articles.title: Kenneth Walker III Reacts to Historic Performance in Chiefs Debut vs. Broncos, 'It Means A Lot'
articles.summary: In his first game as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs, Kenneth Walker III racked up 191 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in a 31-10 victory over the Denver Broncos on Monday night.
articles.body:
In his first game as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs, Kenneth Walker III racked up 191 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in a 31-10 victory over the Denver Broncos on Monday night.

After becoming just the third Chiefs player to run for at least 100 yards in their team debut since 2000, Walker told reporters "it means a lot" to have a strong start against a good opponent.

"It means a lot," he said. "I see the O-line, the way they work in the weight room and the classroom. We showed it in practice, from OTAs to training camp. We just had to come out here and execute and show it."

Kenneth Walker III goes off in Chiefs debut

Walker, who ended last season winning Super Bowl MVP as a member of the Seattle Seahawks, ran for a career-high 173 yards against a Denver defense that allowed the second-fewest rushing yards in the NFL in 2025.

The only other Chiefs players who ran for at least 100 yards in their team debut this century were Kareem Hunt in 2017 and Clyde Edwards-Helaire in 2020.

Walker also scored two touchdowns, including a 60-yard scamper on fourth-and-1 in the third quarter to put the Chiefs up 21-7.

When the Chiefs signed Walker to a three-year, $43 million contract in free agency, they did so in part to take some of the stress off Patrick Mahomes and to make their offense more three-dimensional.

It's safe to say after one game the plan worked to perfection. The Chiefs' 220 rushing yards as a team against the Broncos were their most in a game since Week 6 of the 2020 season against the Buffalo Bills (245).

Kansas City was able to put up 31 points in a game with Mahomes not looking at quite peak form throwing the football in his return from a torn ACL and LCL. He finished 15-of-27 for 184 yards with two touchdowns and one interception.

Mahomes did add 23 yards and a touchdown on seven rushing attempts, so his knee held up well in the regard.

If the Chiefs are going to have a strong rushing attack with Walker leading the way, their offense could get back to being the world-beating unit it was for the first five years of Mahomes' career as a starter.

That's bad news for anyone who thought the Kansas City dynasty ended last season.

articles.title: "All glory and thanks to God": Patrick Mahomes delivers emotional message after Chiefs’ dominant win over Broncos

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had waited nine long months for this moment. After battling through a serious knee injury and months of demanding rehabilitation, the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback finally returned to an NFL game Monday night. The comeback could hardly have gone better. Mahomes helped Kansas City cruise past the Denver Broncos 31-10, then shared a heartfelt message with Chiefs Kingdom after the final whistle.Patrick Mahomes celebrates NFL return after Chiefs winMahomes did not need a perfect performance to make his return memorable.The three-time Super Bowl champion completed 15 of 27 passes and threw two touchdown passes. He also added a rushing touchdown as the Chiefs controlled the game from start to finish at Arrowhead Stadium.There were moments when the quarterback looked like a player still finding his rhythm. That was hardly surprising after spending months away from competitive football. What mattered most was that Mahomes looked healthy, confident and capable of making plays when Kansas City needed him.The bigger story, though, was what the game meant to Mahomes personally.After spending so much time rehabbing, training and waiting for medical clearance, he finally had the chance to do what he had missed most: play football.Speaking after the win, Mahomes explained that his motivation was remarkably simple.“I just wanted to play,” Mahomes said. “I’ve done so much rehab and so much work to put myself in this position. I just wanted to get out there and play. That’s what you do it for.“My guys around me kind of helped me. Whenever I felt like I didn’t play my best football, we were still able to go out there and beat a really good football team pretty well.“It’s because the guys around me stepped up and knew that they’re going to have to help me as I get back into the rhythm of things.”That final point could prove important for the Chiefs as the season develops. Kansas City does not need Mahomes to carry every possession while he works his way back into top form. A strong supporting cast can take some pressure off him.Patrick Mahomes thanks God after Chiefs returnThe emotion continued after Mahomes left the field.Following the Chiefs' convincing victory over Denver, Mahomes took to X to reflect on his return. His post focused less on statistics and more on gratitude, making it clear how much the opportunity meant to him.He wrote:“Want to give all glory and thanks to God! Letting me be out there doing what I love again! ChiefsKingdom this is just the start see yall next week! 🙏⏰”The message arrived at 9:38 a.m. on September 15, after the Chiefs had completed their season-opening win.For Mahomes, the post captured the journey behind his return. A knee injury can turn an NFL season upside down in an instant. The road back is far less glamorous, filled with rehabilitation sessions, strength work and countless hours spent preparing the body to withstand the demands of football again.Now, Mahomes has finally played his first game back.And the result gives Kansas City plenty of reason to feel encouraged. The quarterback may still have some rust to shake off, but the Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a 31-10 win and a healthy Mahomes under center.His message suggested that he sees Monday night as more than a comeback.For Mahomes, it was the beginning of the next chapter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Week 2 Fantasy Football Rankings Overview for All Positions
articles.summary: Week 1 brought its fair share of surprises, both to the NFL world and to fantasy football managers. We saw stars like Ja'Marr Chase and Matthew Stafford fall well short of expectations, while teams like the New York Jets and Arizona Cardinals were unexpectedly good.
articles.body:
Week 1 brought its fair share of surprises, both to the NFL world and to fantasy football managers. We saw stars like Ja'Marr Chase and Matthew Stafford fall well short of expectations, while teams like the New York Jets and Arizona Cardinals were unexpectedly good.

We also saw multiple players—including A.J. Brown, Sam Darnold, Kyler Murray, and Zay Flowers—go down with Week 1 injuries.

While some of what we saw during the opening slate will prove to be an aberration of the 2026 season, we must adjust the fantasy landscape just a bit heading into Week 2.

Here, you'll find early point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for all positions, along with a few sleepers to consider targeting on the waiver wire.

Sleeper: Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints

Budding New Orleans Saints star Tyler Shough is the quarterback to target on the wire this week. The second-year signal-caller had some early hiccups against the Detroit Lions on Sunday but rebounded to have a fantastic overall performance.

Shough tossed a pair of interceptions but also finished with 410 passing yards, three touchdowns, and eight rushing yards.

This week, Shough will face a Baltimore Ravens defense that did appear to be improved in Week 1. However, his scrambling ability, while not heavily utilized against Detroit, gives him a very attractive floor. At worst, he can be claimed and started later in the season.

Shough is rostered in only 22 percent of fantasy leagues.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Sleeper: Kaelon Black, San Francisco 49ers

The San Francisco 49ers aren't about to replace Christian McCaffrey as their lead running back. However, it's clear that they're going to heavily utilize rookie Kaelon Black in a rotational role.

Against the Los Angeles Rams last Thursday, Black logged 14 carries, a catch, and 70 scrimmage yards. This week, he'll face a Miami Dolphins defense that surrendered 130 rushing yards on Sunday.

Black is worth flex-start consideration this week and is definitely worth picking up as a handcuff to McCaffrey. He's currently rostered in just 10.5 percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Dontayvion Wicks, Philadelphia Eagles

This offseason, the Philadelphia Eagles added wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks in a trade with the Green Bay Packers. It didn't take long for Wicks to show exactly why the Eagles were interested in him.

Wicks was arguably Philadelphia's top big-play threat in Sunday's matchup against the rival Washington Commanders. He was targeted four times and finished with two catches for 73 yards and a touchdown.

While Wicks' PPR floor is suspect, he should have a high ceiling against a lackluster Tennessee Titans secondary this week. If he continues to establish himself as a reliable target, he could become a solid flex streamer moving forward.

Wicks is rostered in just seven percent of leagues.

For whatever reason, fantasy managers just don't seem to like Dalton Schultz. The Houston Texans' pass-catcher finished last season as TE10 in PPR leagues, yet was widely ignored in 2026 drafts.

Schultz is currently rostered in only 17.5 percent of fantasy leagues.

On Sunday, Schultz caught four passes for 35 yards during a back-and-forth battle with the Buffalo Bills. This week, he'll face the Cincinnati Bengals in a game that could also see plenty of offensive production.

articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: Cam Ward had a disastrous performance to start his second season
articles.summary: Cam Ward and the Titans had a horrible performance in Week 1.
articles.body:
Cam Ward was bad as a rookie. In most measures, he was worse than J.J. McCarthy last season. Nobody paid it much mind.

The Tennessee Titans didn't play a single standalone game, which helped keep Ward's struggles in the shadows. Those who broke down his play chose to single out impressive highlights and blame the situation around him for a poor season. And it was a poor situation. Ward deserved a pass. But that was with the expectation that a new coaching staff and an upgraded supporting cast would lead to better results.

It's hard to judge anything one game into an NFL season. But a season doesn't offer many better opportunities than facing the New York Jets at home when the talent around you is healthy and fresh for the opener. And Ward was just as bad as he was last season.

Through the first nine possessions of the game, which spanned 55 minutes, the Titans had one field goal, one fumble and seven punts. They had seven first downs, 130 yards and trailed 23-3. Ward had 140 passing yards and that looked a lot better because of one garbage-time drive. He got 57 of his yards and his only touchdown on that drive, after the Jets had practically moved onto next week.

There was also one comical rep in which Ward flipped the ball to himself on a trick play. You can do things like that when everything is going well. This one ended with a quick sack.

"I am very disappointed," Ward said, via the team's site. "We are better than what we showed offensively. We trained a lot this offseason, we had some hard days. It didn't pay off for us today, but it is going to pay off for us eventually, whether it is next week or the week after. We are going to get it rolling."

Are they going to get it rolling? While the Jets have improved on defense, they allowed the highest passer rating in the NFL last season and were 32nd in defensive DVOA . Again, it won't get easier for the Titans or Ward. And they did practically nothing on offense. Next week the Titans host the Eagles and their stellar defense. It could be ugly.

On Sunday, Titans fans booed. First-year head coach Robert Saleh was asked if he had a message to fans who might be apathetic about the team already, just one game into the season. Maybe it's too early for that, but it seemed like the same Titans from a season ago. The coaches changed, many teammates changed. The quarterback remained the same. As did the results.

It's too early to give up on the No. 1 overall pick after 18 starts, but there needs to be some positive signs, and soon. There haven't been any yet. Ward struggled in the preseason — Titans beat writers said Ward did look good in practices — and that poor play carried over to Sunday. Other than draft pedigree, there aren't many tangible reasons to believe in anything better coming up. That's a tough place to be one game into your second season.

Panic meter: Too early to jump ship on Ward, but not too early to be seriously concerned.

Nobody is trying to say Maye has played well lately. The three interceptions he threw in the New England Patriots ' opener were awful. But the criticism of Maye on social media has gone overboard.

Going back to the recent postseason, Maye has had five subpar games in a row. Those games came against the Chargers , Texans , Broncos and two against the Seahawks . The Texans, Broncos and Seahawks have top-five defenses and the Chargers were a top-10 defense in DVOA last season. Half of one, against the Broncos, was played in a blizzard. There were also factors around Maye that weren't great, whether it was the struggling offensive line last season or injuries to A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson in Week 1 this season. But it has become easy and trendy to shred Maye and call him a fraud, so here we are.

Maye had a fantastic 2025 season. It was against an easy schedule in NFL terms, but it's still pro competition. He didn't play in the MAC. He played well enough to deservedly come one vote from winning NFL MVP. He's 24 years old. Maye is and will be fine. He needs to play better than he has lately. Not playing an elite defense every week should help.

Panic meter: Not nearly as much as you'd think, based on social media pitchforks.

The Colts were one of the NFL's darlings in the first half last season, getting off to a great start and being one of the league's best offenses until Daniel Jones tore his Achilles. There wasn't a fast start this season. They lost 41-23 to the Ravens . According to RotoWire , teams that lose by 14 or more points in Week 1 make the playoffs just 18.8% of the time. And losing at home in Week 1 by any margin is a bad sign. Only 21.8% of home Week 1 losers make the playoffs, compared to 29.5% of road losers according to RotoWire.

And it's not just the leaguewide trends. The Colts didn't look good in the opener. Their defense allowed more than 500 yards. Jones had the fourth-worst adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play among all Week 1 quarterbacks. There was never any guarantee Jones would bounce right back after a major injury, and his Week 1 performance was alarming. He had just one run for 4 yards. He didn't pass it well. Nothing looked easy. In a season that is critical for head coach Shane Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard, in terms of their job security, this was an awful start.

Panic meter: Maybe the Ravens are just that good, but the Colts couldn't have been much worse.

Look away, survival pool players . The Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals wasn't shocking just for the loss itself, but how uncompetitive the Chargers were in the game.

The Cardinals clearly outplayed the Chargers. They outgained Los Angeles 393-268. They had more first downs and a better yards per play. It was a 12-point win and that wasn't fluky.

Before being too concerned about the Chargers, remember that odd things happen in Week 1. The Patriots lost to the Raiders at home last season and won the AFC. The Seahawks lost to the 49ers at home and won the Super Bowl. Three of the last 10 champions were 0-1, according to RotoWire.

The Chargers looked poor on both sides of the ball. For now, we'll assume this was the weird Week 1 result we'll be talking about months down the road.

Panic meter: A bad loss, but this seems like a one-off result.

articles.title: Jerry Jones 'Very Optimistic' Cowboys Can Play Better After Loss to Giants in NFL Week 1
articles.summary: Despite a disappointing loss against the New York Giants in Sunday night's season opener, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is confident in his team's ability to bounce back quickly.
articles.body:
Despite a disappointing loss against the New York Giants in Sunday night's season opener, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is confident in his team's ability to bounce back quickly.

During his weekly radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Jones declared that the Cowboys will perform better in Week 2 when they meet the Washington Commanders.

"We're very optimistic that we can play better than we did Sunday night," Jones said, per The Athletic's Jon Machota . "… We caught a Giants team that is much improved and well-coached. … We have our heads down. We will do some things differently this week."

Despite facing a rebuilding Giants team that is entering a new era under head coach John Harbaugh, the Cowboys suffered a 28-20 loss in front of a primetime audience on Sunday Night Football . Star quarterback Dak Prescott was limited to 175 yards and two touchdowns on 22-of-34 passing. He also threw an interception before halftime that Jones said was "definitely the turning point in the game."

Jones went on to add that despite the lackluster showing to start the season, it's up to the Cowboys to address their deficiencies before they return to the field at home against the Commanders.

"We're all very disappointed. Having said that, though, the question is, 'OK, what are we going to do about it?'" Jones said. "The real world is that we are where we thought we were relative to continually working on the things that you saw kick us in the butt [Sunday night]. We're going to continue [working on] that. The very things that, frankly, caused us to not win that ballgame are the things that we should be working on and what we were working on going into the game."

Jones also noted that Dallas has integrated many new faces this offseason, especially on defense. Still, he expressed optimism that the team will fare better against Washington.

"The facts are, we got a lot of new people on defense doing different things then they've been doing. So, that's got to come together," he said. "If we will keep our head down and working on it, it will be better than it was Sunday night."

articles.title: His coach thinks he will be the best quarterback ever. He has a long way to go.
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was not shy when discussing his expectations for starting quarterback Justin Herbert before the season, opting instead to make a very specific — and very bold — claim.
articles.body: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was not shy when discussing his expectations for starting quarterback Justin Herbert before the season, opting instead to make a very specific — and very bold — claim. “Allow me to call my shot, like Babe Ruth pointing his bat over to centerfield. Justin Herbert, when it’s all said and done, when his career comes to an end, I predict he will be known as the greatest, best ever to play the position of quarterback,” Harbaugh said during an appearance on the podcast “The White House with Michael Irvin.” “When it’s all said and done, and his career is finished, we’re going to look back and say, ‘Yep, that’s the best that ever did it.’” Harbaugh, in his third season as the Chargers’ head coach, is known for his quarterback acumen, so his words can’t be immediately dismissed. In college, he coached future first-round picks such as Andrew Luck and J.J. McCarthy. And in the NFL, he brought out the best in Alex Smith and Colin Kaepernick. Herbert, the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft, has long tantalized analysts because of his supreme physical traits, which include athleticism and a cannon of a right arm. To add fuel to the fire, Harbaugh earlier this year hired a new offensive coordinator, former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel, a quarterback guru in his own right who led the Dolphins to great offensive heights for multiple seasons. So a perfect storm was brewing for Herbert to live up to his head coach’s lofty dreams in Week 1. Instead, in a week when offenses dominated the NFL, Los Angeles fell flat, mustering only two touchdowns in a 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. After one report claimed McDaniel was going to explore more of his playbook thanks to Herbert’s physical gifts, the quarterback ended his first start with a pedestrian stat line: 17 of 27 passing for 209 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. On Sunday, Harbaugh described the performance as sloppy. On Monday, he lamented not having the team more prepared. “Now in retrospect, wish I would have played our guys a little bit more in the preseason getting those game-like reps,” Harbaugh told reporters after saying the team committed too many “preseason-type” mistakes. At least in terms of what went wrong, the coach and quarterback are on the same page, as Herbert repeatedly mentioned execution issues Sunday. “We can’t expect to win like that,” Herbert said. “And we have to do better.” While Herbert can’t control the opinions of the masses — or even his own coach — he does occupy a strange space in the NFL quarterback ecosystem. Before the season, The Athletic’s Mike Sando polled 50 coaches and executives as part of his annual QB Tiers ranking, and Herbert took the sixth spot. But Herbert is coming off a season in which he finished only 15th in passer rating. And since 2024, among quarterbacks with a minimum of 500 plays, Herbert is only 17th in adjusted expected points added per play and 20th in success rate, per RBSDM, an advanced analytics site for NFL statistics. McDaniel was supposed to be the coordinator who could bridge the gap between Herbert’s talent and production — particularly after McDaniel drew up high-scoring offenses for Tua Tagovailoa, a quarterback not nearly as physically gifted as Herbert. Whatever the Chargers’ issues are, the offense needs to get on track fast, as their schedule is unforgiving. Over the next two months, Los Angeles will face a gauntlet that includes multiple MVPs (Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson), multiple recent Super Bowl winners (Seattle Seahawks, Kansas City Chiefs), and multiple ferocious defenses (Denver Broncos, Houston Texans). If the Chargers are going to survive such a hellacious stretch, then their quarterback will have to start living up to what his coach (and seemingly most of the NFL) believe he can be.

articles.title: Andy Reid Says ESPN Icon Chris Berman Sent Him 1936 Play Design Used on Kenneth Walker's MNF TD
articles.summary: While they didn't raffle off the chance to be offensive coordinator for a drive, the Kansas City Chiefs did get help from a surprising source on their play design that resulted in a touchdown for Kenneth Walker III in the fourth quarter of Monday's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
While they didn't raffle off the chance to be offensive coordinator for a drive, the Kansas City Chiefs did get help from a surprising source on their play design that resulted in a touchdown for Kenneth Walker III in the fourth quarter of Monday's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters after the game that the play was originally sent to him by ESPN legend Chris Berman before they adapted it to use against the Broncos.

Reid said the play, which featured quarterbacks Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields in the backfield lined up in the three-point stance before the snap, originated in 1936.

Walker, who was lined up on the outside, came back across the field behind the line of scrimmage after the snap and took a forward pitch from Mahomes then ran between a block to get in the end zone.

This was a vintage moment for Reid, who has often taken plays from long ago and revived them at the right time. They used a play from the 1948 Rose Bowl on a fourth-down play in Super Bowl 54 against the San Francisco 49ers.

Reid's creative ingenuity was something that analysts felt was missing in recent years, particularly last season, as a reason to explain in part why the offensive production had fallen off from its peak years.

If Monday night is any indication, Reid appears to have gotten that spark back. That could be bad news for the rest of the NFL that was hoping the Chiefs may not be the dominant force they were during the period when they won three Super Bowls in five seasons from 2019 to '23.

articles.title: NFL, MLB, NBA, other pro leagues band together to crack down on betting-related harassment; WNBPA slams exclusion
articles.summary: Most professional sports leagues now have partnerships with betting operators.
articles.body:
The NFL, NBA, MLS, NHL and MLB are banding together to crack down on betting-related harassment of players, coaches and families in their respective sports. The leagues — and their respective unions — put out a joint statement Tuesday suggesting punishments for those who engage in harassment due to betting.

The statement was written to address individuals who "direct threatening and harassing messages toward players, coaches and their families via social media and in-person interactions."

"Threatening the safety of an athlete or their family members over a sports bet crosses a bright ethical and criminal line, and it is entirely unacceptable."

After laying out the issue, the leagues suggested a number of actions the State Gaming Commissions and Regulatory Authorities could take to curb that type of behavior from fans.

• Mandatory lifetime ban: Sportsbooks and mobile betting operators should create clear rules that could result in lifetime bans for fans who harass or issue threats of violence against athletes or others around the game.

• Steamlined reporting mechanisms: Sportsbooks and mobile betting operators should create a clear way to report evidence to the proper authorities.

• Operator accountability: Sportsbooks and mobile betting operators should proactively monitor flag and ban accounts linked to abusive behavior.

NFL, MLB, NBA, others partnered with betting operators

The statement comes after multiple professional sports leagues have partnered with sportsbooks or betting operators in recent months. In August, the NFL announced partnerships with FanDuel, DraftKings and Fanatics Betting and Gaming. MLB has been partnered with FanDuel since 2023 and its teams have sought partnerships with other prediction markets . The NBA has a full webpage dedicated to listing off its official gaming partners and operators.

WNBPA issues its own statement criticizing NBA

The WNBA, notably, was not included in the statement. WNBPA executive director Terri Carmichael Jackson said that was not the union's choice, saying the NBA chose not to include the WNBPA in the joint statement.

"It is deeply disappointing that, given the very public and troubling incidents of betting-related harassment experienced by our members over the past several seasons, the NBA determined that WNBA players did not warrant inclusion in a joint position statement intended to address this very issue."

Like the NBA, the WNBA also has a webpage listing off its partnerships with betting operators.

The rise of legalized sports betting has resulted in numerous athletes speaking out on harassment they've received as a result of gambling .

articles.title: Jets Receive Brutal Injury News on Minkah Fitzpatrick Ahead of Packers Game
articles.summary: The New York Jets kicked off the 2026 NFL season in style, defeating the Tennessee Titans 23-10 to move to 1-0.Now, as the Jets shift their focus to Week 2 a...
articles.body:
The New York Jets kicked off the 2026 NFL season in style, defeating the Tennessee Titans 23-10 to move to 1-0.

Now, as the Jets shift their focus to Week 2 and a highly anticipated matchup against the Green Bay Packers , they will be without a crucial piece of their defense.

After exiting the game against the Titans with a groin injury, Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick did not return, and on Tuesday, they received an update on his status.

Jets Receive Brutal Injury News on Fitzpatrick

While it's not the worst-case scenario of going on IR or missing a lengthy portion of the season, the injury will sideline Fitzpatrick for at least 2-3 weeks, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.

The Jets rely heavily on the leadership and mix of youth and veteran experience they boast defensively, and right in the center of all that is Fitzpatrick on the backend.

At least from what we saw on Sunday, backup safety Andre Cisco will likely step into the role of starter alongside Dane Belton.

However, DB Malachi Moore will also see an increased number of snaps with Fitzpatrick sidelined.

The Jets drafted Moore in the fourth round of last year's NFL Draft, and he started 14 of their 17 games. Cisco enters his sixth season and second with New York after spending his first four years with the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Cisco played eight games for the Jets last season and started every one at safety. He has started 55 of the 72 games he's played in during his career.

articles.title: Veteran referee Clete Blakeman assigned to Week 2 Saints-Ravens game
articles.summary: Veteran referee Clete Blakeman has been assigned to Week 2's Saints-Ravens game. His crew ranked fifth in penalty flags thrown last year.
articles.body:
Much of the attention on the officiating in the New Orleans Saints ' season opener has rightfully gone to a bad rule that erased a defensive touchdown, which could have kept the game from going to overtime -- and secured a Week 1 upset win against the Detroit Lions . Former referees, rules analysts, and NFL officials all agree the play was ruled correctly as written, but that doesn't change the fact it's a bad rule . That it's both rarely come up before (if ever) and that it means a ball traveling backwards could be defined as a forward pass is ridiculous. Tear that page out of the rulebook.

Nevertheless, we're on to Week 2. Veteran referee Clete Blakeman has been assigned to Week 2's road game with the Baltimore Ravens , per Football Zebras . Blakeman is one of the most experienced officials in the game today, having worked for two years as a field judge before being promoted to lead his own crew back in 2010. He has refereed 16 games for the Saints, who went 9-7 in those matchups. The Ravens are 11-5 in 16 games with Blakeman at referee.

Blakeman's crew was one of the NFL's fastest to throw a penalty marker last season, with 218 fouls called in 17 games (16.5 per week), fifth-most. They also assessed the seventh-most penalty yardage (1,720) with 20 more penalties going against visitors than home teams. Like most crews, their most-common fouls are for offensive holding, false starts, and defensive pass interference. Last week Blakeman's crew tied with Alan Eck's group, who officiated the Saints-Lions game, with 14 penalties. That ranked fourth-fewest. The New Orleans offensive line can't afford many mistakes this week. Let's see if they show up.

articles.title: Commanders WR Antonio Williams nominated for rookie award
articles.summary: Commanders rookie Antonio Williams had four receptions for 64 yards and a touchdown against the Eagles on Sunday
articles.body:
Commanders receiver Antonio Williams didn't play much but did a ton with the time allotted. The third-round rookie had four receptions for 64 yards and a late fourth-quarter that put Washington within a (ultimately failed) 2-point conversion in Sunday's 24-22 loss to Philadelphia .

He did all that despite playing 26 offensive snaps and running just 10 routes .

That's why Williams was nominated for the Rookie of the Week honor for Week 1, which is selected via fan vote. He's competing against Tampa Bay linebacker Josiah Trotter, Tennessee linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. and Miami receiver Caleb Douglas.

Williams was solid all game. He created separation well and made an excellent TD catch on his final highlight of the day.

articles.title: Eagles News: Landon Dickerson replacement options
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 9/15/26.
articles.body:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

With Landon Dickerson expected to go on injured reserve, the Eagles need a new starting left guard. Drew Kendall should and likely will be be the first man up. I know people love Willie Lampkin — and I'm one of them! — but he wasn't taking first-team reps this summer. It was Kendall filling in at LG whenever Dickerson missed time. Kendall lacks a ton of experience at guard; he only played center in college. But he's been learning the position since entering the NFL last year. I don't like the idea of moving Cam Jurgens to left guard and changing two starting spots on the offensive line. How do you think the team should handle this situation?

Let's get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Second-year offensive lineman Drew Kendall is expected to replace Dickerson, unless the Eagles decide on another configuration that could shift center Cam Jurgens to guard. Willie Lampkin is also in play for either job, although Kendall is the likely first interior lineman up. Kendall played center exclusively in college, while Jurgens' first season as a starter in the NFL was at right guard. Jurgens also struggled against Washington on Sunday. Like Dickerson, he played through injury during the Super Bowl LIX run in 2025 and returned the following season following back surgery. He never looked 100%. Dickerson's career, dating back to college, has been injury-plagued. He had multiple ACL tears, ankle surgeries, and other ailments during his time at Florida State and Alabama. The Eagles drafted him in the second round despite the medical red flags. He quickly became one of the NFL's best interior linemen, though, and earned three straight Pro Bowl nods from 2022-24. But the injuries mounted, and while Dickerson missed only a handful of games in his first five seasons, it increasingly affected his performance. The Eagles' changes to their offensive scheme this offseason were expected to affect Dickerson the most out of the starting five O-linemen. The wide-zone blocking requires more athletic and agile blockers.

I'd expect Drew Kendall to get the nod to start in Dickerson's place this Sunday against the Tennessee Titans . Eagles general manager Howie Roseman offered a now-telling admission during a news conference last month closing out training camp that, if he'd been given truth serum going into the summer, he'd have said the interior offensive line depth was the thing he was most worried about. Kendall, along with training camp darling Willie Lampkin and sixth-round rookie Micah Morris, each had strong enough camps to quiet that worry for Roseman and Kendall seems the most ready to jump up the depth chart. "If any of you would've given me a truth serum and said, 'What are you looking for in training camp?' It would be how our interior offensive line depth panned out," Roseman said. "Those young guys and the growth that they showed, their ability to play in the passing game, in the run game. I mean, really, really excited about those guys, about being able to have those guys, being able to develop those guys, but at the same time, have confidence that if those guys need to play, that they're ready to play."

Drew Kendall to center. Perhaps the loss of Dickerson will make the Eagles shuffle their line. Because Kendall is a more natural center, the Eagles could elect to plug him there and move Cam Jurgens to guard. Jurgens is a two-time Pro Bowl center but was a full-time starter at guard during the 2023 season. Former offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland normally tried to avoid shuffling the line like this because he thought it weakened them at two spots. But Stoutland isn't their OL coach anymore and Chris Kuper might have different feelings on how to go about finding their best starting five.

This means Drew Kendall becomes the LG. Willie Lampkin is now the top backup interior OL. Jake Majors or John Ojukwu could be promoted from the practice squad for depth. Ojukwu has more experience. Both guys are good scheme fits. Rookie Micah Morris is talented, but I think he's more of a long term solution than someone they would play right away. Howie Roseman talked this summer about how his big concern in the offseason was interior OL depth. The Eagles had several guys step up and perform well. Now comes the real test. I'm happy that Dickerson and the team took decisive action. If you know he's not healthy, get him out of there. Give Kendall a chance to show what he can do. Is this the end of Dickerson's career? It very well could be. Hopefully some time off will help him to heal and he can get back on the field one more time. No one wants to go out on a bad game.

There were a lot of things to address coming out of the Philadelphia Eagles Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders , but arguably the biggest concern was starting left guard Landon Dickerson. Just one day later, the three-time Pro Bowler is expected to be heading to injured reserve, which means he will miss at least the next four games.

The first week of the NFL season is just about over, and wow do we have some NFC East action to discuss! To start… the New York Giants actually did it. They announced that maybe this time finally is different as they completely dismantled the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. Earlier in the day, the Philadelphia Eagles withstood a rally from the Washington Commanders for more of the same as far as recent history is concerned. How are we feeling about all four teams as we move on into the actual season? RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed!

5) Eagles (1-0): The Eagles' defense kept the Commanders from doing much of anything until the fourth quarter, and Jalen Hurts made enough plays to win the Eagles the game, but 10 first downs was the second-fewest in the NFL Week 1, behind only the Broncos . The Titans had 11. The Dolphins had 13. Even the Browns had 15. And the Eagles played against one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Not good enough. Last week: 3.

There were new schemes, new coaches, but ultimately a continuation of a year-old problem. Jalen Hurts' second-half heroics allow new Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion to solve second-half stalls in the safety of the win column — much like his predecessor did until the stalls eventually did him in. The 2025 Eagles were the only team in coach Nick Sirianni's tenure to finish a season with a negative second-half scoring margin (-7). The 2026 Eagles own a minus-3 second-half point differential after Week 1. Debuts offer some forgiveness. So do wins. Mannion, a first-time play caller, will look back on a mostly brutal 20-play sequence that portrayed the antithesis of the "aggressive" approach Sirianni said they'd intended entering the second half. "We don't think about taking our foot off the gas," Sirianni said afterward. Not intentionally. Not unless they're bleeding the clock while nursing a lead with four minutes left in the game. But the Eagles went three-and-out on their first three drives of the second half. Several offensive players said Mannion wanted to turn to their wide zone run game after establishing a 14-9 halftime lead. The Washington Commanders thwarted the plan by sending preemptive pressure against offensive looks with a small sample of tendencies.

11) The Eagles didn't start the season like a well-oiled machine, but they were able to rely on their defense for a good portion of Sunday's opener and received some timely contributions from Jalen Hurts and the offense to outlast the Commanders. Philadelphia can be proud of starting 1-0, but the Eagles likely understand they'll need to be better over the long haul to achieve their goals.

As we continue to celebrate the Eagles' first win of the new season, the team's cheerleading squad is introducing some new members. One is a nurse at Jefferson Health. The Eagles have 32 cheerleaders. In addition to being accomplished athletic dancers, they have a variety of day jobs that include four in healthcare.

Ben VanSumeren could be the Chiefs ' first pure fullback to take the field since Michael Burton in 2022. The fourth-year player entered the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles as an undrafted free agent linebacker from Michigan. Listed at 6 feet 2 inches tall and 258 pounds, VanSumeren switched to the fullback position in 2025, appearing in one game for the Eagles and spending this summer with the Buffalo Bills before being cut.

That was different. Yes, the simple fact that the New York Giants won a season-opener on Sunday night was different. The Giants had lost six of seven season-opening games against the Dallas Cowboys prior to Sunday's impressive 28-20 victory. They had started 10 of the 13 previous seasons 0-2 or worse. So, sure, Sunday was different in that sense. What was really different, though, was the atmosphere inside MetLife Stadium throughout the night. Fans of the Cowboys, Philadelphia Eagles, and other teams have made a habit in recent years of infiltrating and taking over the Giants' home stadium. Not Sunday night. Maybe it was emotions from the 9/11 commemorations by the Giants. Maybe it was the beginning of the John Harbaugh Era following a summer of optimistic reporting about the state of the team. Maybe it was the introductions of Malik Nabers , who played, and Odell Beckham Jr. , who officially returned. Whatever it was, the atmosphere inside MetLife Stadium was electric.

QB Jayden Daniels never looked comfortable. Maybe that was Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio getting him rattled. Maybe that was having a new center he barely worked with throughout the summer and maybe that was a new coordinator who didn't do him any favors in play calling. Whatever the case, he looked flustered and a bit indecisive. He did have some big throws and runs later in the game, and I think things between him and Blough will eventually click.

Stock Down: Division dominance. Objectively speaking, the Cowboys have beaten up on the NFC East for much of the Dak Prescott era. Specifically, they have pushed around the Giants whenever they wanted. This was just one game to be clear, but it was not the meaningless contest that Dallas lost to New York in Week 18 last year. The Cowboys gave this game all of their might and the new-look Giants humbled them mightily. Next week will bring another test of this variety. The Washington Commanders took the Philadelphia Eagles the distance a few hours before the Cowboys failed against the Giants, and one of Washington and Dallas will fall to 0-2 by this time next week. Who will it be?

Life as a punt gunner can be hard in football, and particularly in the NFL. The basic job description reads like something out of "American Gladiators." Sprint 50 to 60 yards downfield while tracking a punt and either tackle one of the more elusive players on the opposing team after they field it, or have the awareness to track the football in flight, see where it lands, and touch it down inside the opponent's five-yard line. And if you botch either of those, not only will you become a meme overnight, but you will definitely hear about it in Monday's film review session. Oh, and adding to the difficulty is that you will often be up against at least one, sometimes two, players on the other side of the ball, trying their best to prevent you from even getting ten yards downfield.

articles.title: 5 Major Sports Leagues and Players Associations Ask for Protections from Sports Bettors' Threats
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Five professional sports leagues and their players associations have aligned forces to ask for protections for players and staff who face threats and harassment from sports bettors.
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Five professional sports leagues and their players associations have aligned forces to ask for protections for players and staff who face threats and harassment from sports bettors.

The Associated Press obtained a copy of the letter sent Tuesday to gambling regulators in 35 states and the District of Columbia. In the letter, the NFL, Major League Baseball, NBA, Major League Soccer and the NHL and the leagues' players associations asked that rules be established to permanently revoke betting privileges for anyone found to have threatened or "abusively harassed" any professional or amateur athlete, coach, official or team personnel."

The letter to state gambling regulators cited "the escalating threat facing professional players, coaches, and officials, the continued harassment and violent threats from sports bettors."

"While the expansion of legal, state-regulated sports betting has brought new ways for fans to engage with their favorite sports, it has also introduced some negative consequences for players and other personnel involved with professional sporting events," the leagues and players associations wrote. "Too often, individuals who lose sports bets direct threatening and harassing messages toward players coaches and their families via social media and in-person interactions.

"Threatening the safety of an athlete or their family members over a sports bet crosses a bright ethical and criminal line and it is entirely unacceptable. It is critical that state and local leaders safeguard the participants of sports at all levels."

The letter noted that Ohio, West Virginia, Louisiana and Wyoming already exclude "bad actors" from licensed sportsbooks and mobile applications. The letter asks for broader protections from the other 35 states and District of Columbia, which do not have similar laws or protections in place since the Supreme Court paved the way for gambling legalization in 2018.

"We call on all state gaming commissions and state policymakers to promptly adopt uniform rules and legislative guardrails to help address this behavior," the leagues and players associations wrote, asking state-regulated sportsbooks and mobile betting operators "to permanently revoke wagering privileges for any individual verified to have abusively harassed or issued threats of violence against any professional or amateur athlete, coach, official, team personnel or their respective families."

articles.title: Za'Darius Smith Paying For His Church Congregation to Attend Falcons Home Opener
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons defensive end Za'Darius Smith told reporters Tuesday that he is paying for his church's congregation to attend his team's home opener against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons defensive end Za'Darius Smith told reporters Tuesday that he is paying for his church's congregation to attend his team's home opener against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

"This weekend I'm bringing my church up. I know that's something that my mom always wanted, so I got a Greyhound bus pulling up this weekend to my church to bring them up for the game," Smith said.

"So that's gonna be big for me, man. So if y'all see them on the sidelines, just give them a couple words and ask questions about the young Z (chuckles), if you don't mind.

"Excited for that, man, and can't wait. I think we got the tickets now, it's at 45 people? Yeah, I got everybody some T-shirts, gonna feed them good, got a little envelope. I'm gonna put something nice in there for them, man. So, I know my mom, she's smiling down, gonna be happy for this one, man, so I can't wait."

Smith's mother, Sharon Smith, passed away in February. During a meeting with reporters last month, Smith revealed he left his old team, the Philadelphia Eagles, last October after receiving news from his mother's doctor that she did not have long to live. As Smith also told reporters, his grandmother and father recently died as well.

"My mom—rest her soul, man—she always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons," Smith said.

According to Falcons senior reporter Will McFadden , Smith's church is Harrison Street Baptist in Greenville, Alabama, which is the three-time Pro Bowler's hometown and about a three-hour drive southwest of Atlanta.

Smith signed a one-year, $6 million deal with the Falcons last August.

Sunday's kickoff between the Falcons and Panthers is set for 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: John Harbaugh has already given the Giants something they haven't had in years  — hope
articles.summary: The Giants won their season opener for the first time since 2022.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — On the ride from the Meadowlands back into Manhattan, hours after the Giants had just decimated the Cowboys on national television, I heard an unfamiliar note in the radio host's voice as he discussed the Giants: pride .

Bluster, defiance, outrage — these are your go-to emotions for New York sports radio. But this host — I beg your pardon, sir, I didn't get your name but it was 2 a.m. and I was in an Uber — declared that under new head coach John Harbaugh, this is a team that Giants fans can be proud of, and he's exactly right. The host then went on to say that this is a team that could go all the way, but we'll chalk that part up to post-victory exuberance.

The pride thing, though, that's dead-on. Yes, all the usual "it's just one game" caveats exist, but let's be honest here — didn't the Giants just feel like a different team on Sunday night? Disciplined, determined, opportunistic, relentless. Yes, the Cowboys didn't exactly show up prepared — we'll get to that in a moment — but the Giants took advantage of every opportunity presented to them, and seized a few that weren't.

"This was really special because these guys, these players, these guys who have believed from the beginning, they don't bat an eye," Harbaugh said Sunday night. "They just try to do the right thing every single day. They try to be on point. And even when they're not on point, they're going to bounce back and make it right. Maybe there is a mistake. Maybe there is a false start. They find a way to make a play and erase the mistake and make it right and make it better."

This is a team that held Dallas — a trendy preseason Super Bowl favorite, and the favorite coming into Sunday night — to a three-and-out on the Cowboys' opening series, and then immediately marched down the field to score a touchdown on the first series of the season.

This is a team that punted the ball away with 1:50 remaining on the clock, snagged a ridiculous interception on what should have been a throwaway, then raced to another touchdown in 29 seconds.

This is a team that mounted two more eight-minute-plus touchdown drives in the second half, then held the ball for the final 5:21 of the game, utterly strangling the hope right out of the Cowboys.

Score fast, score slow. Score running the same damn play five separate times on a single drive, as the Giants did in the fourth quarter with a Jaxson Dart-to-Devin Singletary flare-out into the left flat. Score with the kind of celebration that lights up social media, like Cam Skattebo 's first-quarter, physician-defying flip.

For a franchise that had won a total of 13 games the last three seasons combined, Sunday night was nothing short of an epiphany. With a single game, Harbaugh has swept away years of futility and instilled a mindset of expectation and self-respect that extends from the field to the stands and back.

"We have so much respect for Coach [Harbaugh], and this team will do whatever he says because we have all the faith that he's going to put us in the best situation," Dart said Sunday night. "The identity of a team starts at the top. It starts with how he's conducted himself, with how he's created a tough team."

That extends even to tackling his own players. Malik Nabers , so uncertain of his playing status on Sunday night that he didn't even bring his family to the game, was in the middle of walkthroughs when Harbaugh, out of nowhere, tackled him .

The message: you're ready to take a hit. And he was; Nabers, coming off a torn ACL, had six receptions on nine targets for 69 yards.

"It was all in fun. Got a lot of laughs," Harbaugh joked on Monday. "Some guys gave me a sideways look. Some of the players were like, 'What are you doing?' So, it was good."

This is unfamiliar territory for the Giants and their fans as of late; the team hasn't made the playoffs since the 2022 season. But before Big Blue Nation starts making February hotel reservations in Los Angeles , keep in mind that Dallas — particularly the woeful, overmatched Cowboy defense — deserves a Best Supporting Actor nomination for making the Giants look so good.

"How you play this week is not going to be good enough to win next week," Harbaugh said Monday. "How we played [Sunday] night will not win the game next Monday night. It won't be good enough. So, we've got to improve."

If the Giants can in fact improve on their performance Sunday night — starting with a Monday night road game against the Rams — New York sports talk radio is going to be a lot of fun over the next few months.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injury Timeline Updated in New Rumors amid 'Unique' Issue for Seahawks QB
articles.summary: Sam Darnold could potentially be out as many as six weeks due to the soft-tissue glute injury he suffered in the Seattle Seahawks' Week 1 win over the New England Patriots.
articles.body:
Sam Darnold could potentially be out as many as six weeks due to the soft-tissue glute injury he suffered in the Seattle Seahawks' Week 1 win over the New England Patriots.

According to Albert Breer of SI.com, "Darnold's injury is unique—to the glute tendon and the hip joint—and for that reason the Seahawks are uncertain of when he'll return. ... one estimate I heard pegged Darnold's at three to six weeks, but, again, I can say that the team itself doesn't have any firm timetable."

Darnold, 29, only played one series before leaving the game and not returning due to the injury. He was replaced by veteran Drew Lock, who finished 16-of-22 for 187 yards and a touchdown—and ran twice for 13 yards—in the 13-10 comeback win.

On Thursday, head coach Mike Macdonald said the team got " really, really good news " on Darnold's injury but didn't offer a timeline for his return.

"The hip is intact, and it's good," he added. "It's more like a muscle thing. So that's good. So how long that is? We don't know yet."

It remains to be seen if Darnold will end up on injured reserve, which would require him to miss at least four games. Either way, his absence means an extended run for Lock, who was up to the task in Week 1.

"Drew provides a cool confidence, a loosened focusedness to the whole equation, which you need," Macdonald said. "Since he's got here, I feel like he's just played really great football, in practice and the preseason. We saw what he could do last night, and if he has to play again, then we expect the same moving forward."

Seattle will be on the road this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, a team coming off a 26-14 upset over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1.

articles.title: Retired NFL star falls into social media hole by comparing Mike Vrabel scandal and Jonathan Cooper arrest
articles.summary: Justin Simmons criticized ESPN for mentioning Jonathan Cooper's NFL suspension during the Broncos-Chiefs game, sparking sharp social media pushback.
articles.body: Justin Simmons was an outstanding NFL safety, collecting second-team All-Pro honors four times during his nine-year career. However, now retired, Simmons should probably be more careful with his social media commentary. That's because Simmons stepped on something of an online landmine Monday night while he was watching his former Denver Broncos team play the Kansas City Chiefs. During the broadcast, ESPN's Joe Buck noted that Broncos' linebacker Jonathan Cooper was not in the lineup because he's currently suspended on the NFL exempt list while he awaits a Nov. 10 trial on four charges, including felony second-degree assault by strangulation of his former girlfriend. 3 NFL STARS HIT COMMISSIONER'S EXEMPT LIST AFTER OFFSEASON FILLED WITH LEGAL TROUBLE The broadcast apparently triggered Simmons, who took to his X account to make a comparative point. The former NFL great complained that ESPN was mentioning his former teammate during the broadcast but the situation between New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and former reporter Dianna Russini wasn't discussed on TV. NBC REMINDS PREGAME VIEWERS ABOUT MIKE VRABEL-DIANNA RUSSINI SCANDAL COACH AND PATRIOTS WANT TO FORGET So, social media simply moved on without pushback whatsoever. Yeah, right. Multiple people basically told off Simmons. They made the point that even if Vrabel's relationship with Russini was perhaps morally wrong, if one assumes it reached heights that have not been proven, it wasn't illegal. Vrabel has been put before the court of public opinion for the relationship, but there are no allegations of abuse that will be heard in a court of law. The analogy between Cooper and Vrabel is flawed at best. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! So, Simmons found himself in a hole he jumped into. Then, unfortunately for him, he proceeded to dig himself deeper. "That’s absolute bs btw," Simmons wrote in an ensuing post as a media critic. "Shame on all of the production on Monday night football and the crew. You’re supposed to call the game. Coop isn’t playing the game and isn’t on the sidelines. "The MNF crew is paid to cover THE GAME not the players who are not playing or even at the game." That's an interesting use of capital letters. Let's go with that flow: Simmons is apparently of the opinion that, since his former teammate isn't playing nor on the sideline – BECAUSE HE WAS ARRESTED ON CHARGES OF CHOKING HIS FORMER GIRLFRIEND AND THEN SUSPENDED BY THE NFL – the broadcast should not mention his name and situation. So any person not in the stadium is apparently off limits from discussion, per Simmons. That apparently should include a person who would be playing if he hadn't done something for which he was arrested, charged with and apologized before he got lawyered up and pleaded not guilty. NFL FACING A DOMESTIC VIOLENCE EPIDEMIC THIS OFFSEASON WITH ARREST OF RAMS LINEMAN THE LATEST CASE Simmons is a bright individual of great character. He played well and was a leader throughout his career, which means he rarely faced public criticism. He was clearly caught off guard, then, when fans challenged his views on Vrabel and Cooper and on ESPN's right to address the matter during its broadcast. "I have hella people in my comments (mainly Pats fans) saying an affair is not the same as an ALLEGED conviction," Simmons wrote. "Which is true. However, last time I checked MNF or any network hosting a game is supposed to talk about just that THE GAME not players who aren’t there or even playing." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That is obviously not correct. And what's worse, the premise all this is based on is also incorrect. That's because when the New England Patriots opened their season against the Seattle Seahawks, Vrabel's situation was addressed on national television. NBC even included the Russini-Vrabel scandal in an illustrated timeline of the Patriots' offseason. So, yes, Vrabel's situation was discussed on TV and that was the right thing to do – just like it was perfectly correct for Cooper's situation to be mentioned on Monday Night Football. articles.title: NFL Week 1 proper reactions: Rams panic, Bears hype and Chargers doubts need patience after one game
articles.summary: NFL Week 1 overreactions are in full swing, from the Rams missing the playoffs to the Bears offense averaging 40 points per game all season.
articles.body: The NFL is officially back! All 32 teams have now played exactly one game. Yet, people are going to act like that one out of 17 games is plenty of information to inform us about how the rest of the season will go. It's not. Like, at all. NFL WEEK 1 TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS FLASH CONTENDER UPSIDE, BEARS EXPLODE AND PACKERS COLLAPSE There's arguably no bigger overreaction week on the entire sports calendar than the week between Week 1 in the NFL and Week 2 in the NFL. After months of practically zero information, we finally saw teams on the field playing games that matter. But we must remember that Week 1 accounts for 5.9% of the entire season. People in the sports media are going to arrive at wild conclusions based on that minuscule sample size. What if you hired a home inspector for a house you wanted to buy and the inspector came back and said, "Hey, here's 5.9% of my report on this house and nothing more. You ready to make an offer?" But here we are, every season, making decisions based on less than 6% of the information. Nonsense. Let's take a look at some of the vast overreactions seen across the landscape and break them down. The Rams are going to miss the playoffs Of course, this is a major overreaction. The Rams entered the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl, rightfully so, and it seems like everyone is quickly jumping off the bandwagon. Rich Eisen Show producer and on-air contributor Chris Brockman predicted the Rams’ "dream team" would follow the 2011 Eagles and miss the playoffs. There are two problems with this overreaction. The first, and most obvious one, is that it was one game against a good divisional opponent in Australia. Honestly, the Rams were way too cocky going into the game and traveling across the globe 28 hours prior to kickoff was a clear miscalculation. The 49ers went to Australia a week in advance to adapt to the weather and time change. INTRODUCING OUTKICK'S FIRST ORIGINAL ANIMATED SERIES, 'SPORTS TALK WITH CAL MCCALLISTER' The second is that the Rams weren't really at full strength. Aaron Donald didn't play, and Myles Garrett played through a lingering knee issue and is now out for at least four games. Los Angeles didn't generate much pass rush and didn't sack Brock Purdy a single time. That's not going to continue throughout the season. Also, sometimes a team can get caught drinking its own Kool-Aid. No team entered the season with more hype, with some calling them a "super team" where a Super Bowl seemed like the only option. If anything, Week 1's disastrous result might have been the best thing that could have happened. The Rams got an early wake-up call and I expect them to bounce back in a big way over the next few games. The Bears offense is going to be historic The Bears obviously looked great in Week 1, dropping a team-record 59 points in a season opener. Caleb Williams showed off his athleticism and playmaking abilities throughout the afternoon, and Bears fans have reasons to be excited. Bucky Brooks posited that Chicago might average 40 points per game, which would easily set the record for points in a season. But let's pump the brakes just a tad, shall we? First, the Panthers defense isn't exactly a juggernaut. The team gave up some big numbers last season, including 42 to New England and 40 to Buffalo. In addition, Week 1 scoring was up big across the board. Teams don't play their starters much during the preseason which puts defenses at a big disadvantage. A lot of these guys have barely hit any opponents at full speed since last season and practices have gotten much less physical due to concussion and injury concerns. Chicago also benefited from several positive luck factors. The Panthers turned the ball over three times and committed 11 penalties for 84 yards. The Bears converted all four red zone drives into touchdowns and picked up 10-of-14 third downs. Yes, that's what good offenses do, but that ridiculous efficiency is unsustainable over 17 games. Then, there was the large number of big plays. Three different Bears (Williams, D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai) all had at least one carry of at least 29 yards and four different pass catchers (Kalif Raymond, Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, and Cole Kmet) had at least one reception that went for 20+ yards. Again, great offenses produce explosive plays, but this was an outlier. The Bears are going to be good, and the offense is going to score points, but we shouldn't set the expectation at 40 points scored per game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Mike McDaniel–Justin Herbert pairing was a mistake The Chargers looked terrible in a Week 1 upset loss against the Arizona Cardinals as nine-point home favorites. The Cardinals blocked a punt, intercepted Justin Herbert and held Los Angeles to just 117 yards of offense in the second half. Mike McDaniel’s offense was supposed to unlock even more from Herbert, but it produced only two scoring drives, and one was aided by a 48-yard pass-interference penalty. That kind of debut makes it tempting to declare the McDaniel-Herbert pairing a failure after one game. To be clear, I'm not declaring that this team is destined for great things, but burying them after Week 1 is also a mistake. McDaniel's offense is unique, and it takes time to get used to, especially for offensive linemen. The Chargers have two stud tackles, Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt, but are breaking in an entirely new interior offensive line, including a rookie center. They made a lot of mistakes, but they will improve as the season goes along. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Remember that Tua Tagovailoa thrived under McDaniel for multiple seasons and there's no reason to think that Herbert can't have more success than Tagovailoa. I do have concerns about the team's receiver corps, since the Dolphins had Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle, but Ladd McConkey is great and if they can get moderate production from the likes of Tre Harris and Quentin Johnston along with contributions from tight ends David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden, the offense will be fine. That all being said, the Chargers clearly had too much hype coming into the season. While I don't think they're nearly as bad as they looked against Arizona, this doesn't appear to be a team that will seriously challenge for AFC supremacy, either. The Chargers might have been overhyped, but one bad Sunday doesn’t make McDaniel the wrong coordinator for Herbert. To close, I'm going to share a few overreactions that might not be overreactions at all: SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER OK, that's it for Week 1. Remember that we've still got 94% of the season to play, so don't get too excited or too disappointed. Unless you're a Dolphins, Browns or Titans fan, in which case you guys should start thinking about 2027.

articles.title: Examining 5 teams that could be trade candidates for Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Steelers and CB Joey Porter Jr. appear to be at loggerheads over his contract status. If they decide to trade him, here are five teams that could make se...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. are beyond the posturing stage. Trade talk is already in the air, and neither side appears to be trying to waft it away.

The hangup is Porter's contract. He's in the final year of his rookie deal, earning $3.92 million this season, with a $4.92 million cap number. Porter and the Steelers never felt particularly close to an extension, especially after the Seahawks' Devon Witherspoon and the Patriots' Christian Gonzalez agreed on deals that made them the two highest-paid corners in the league.

The 26-year-old Porter is reportedly seeking $30 million plus with his next deal. The Steelers opted to make Porter a healthy inactive in Week 1 while the impasse remains. Barring a quick resolution, a trade could be on the table.

We don't see a lot of young, difference-making cornerbacks traded during the season, but it does happen. Sauce Gardner is the most recent example last season, costing the Colts two future first-round picks and a young player.

That price was high, and Porter's contract status likely would lower that price some, but it signals just how important impact players can be at that position. The 6-foot-2, 193-pound Porter has never made a Pro Bowl and has only three interceptions in three seasons, but his 31 passes defended are a very respectable number — and a key indicator of his ability to make plays on the ball.

With both sides dug in, a trade feels more likely now than ever. If so, which teams could be interested? Let's dig in on the possibilities.

They're atop my list for myriad reasons.

First, it's a scheme fit. Porter is best as a man cornerback, and the Lions were third in man-coverage rate (32%) a year ago. Their man rate was lower in Week 1, with SumerSports charting it at 26%, but you can likely chalk that up to being shorthanded in the secondary. They've already cut Terrion Arnold, and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. is hurt, which has been a chronic problem.

Second, they have the flexibility to do it. The Lions recently restructured the deals of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Penei Sewell and sit almost $39 million under the salary cap for this season. Brad Holmes has never shied away from a bold stroke as general manager, and there are reports that Detroit has already made a call on Porter. The Lions have all their draft picks for 2027, plus a little more, so they could afford the price tag if the Steelers ask for a first-rounder and more for Porter.

The Lions started D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin against the Saints, with Roger McCreary and rookie Keith Abney filling in, and they almost fell under the weight of New Orleans' second-half comeback in Week 1. They need help in the secondary, and this is a Lions team that believes it can be back in the playoff mix. They'd hate to see the secondary break down late in the season again, so the motivation to upgrade has to be there.

And though Porter, who is Pittsburgh through and through as the son of the Steelers' longtime linebacker, has no direct connection to the city of Detroit, there is a fun bit of history involving the Porter family and the city: Dad holding a 5-year old Joey Jr. on Ford Field after the Steelers won Super Bowl XL.

If this trade happens, we demand the photo recreation be shot 20-plus years later.

The Cowboys were sold as a team ready to make their move this season, armed with a loaded offense and a defense that's ready to step up in weight class. Sadly, neither unit performed up to snuff in the Week 1 loss at the Giants.

Do they chalk it up to early growing pains? Or will this make the Cowboys more likely to continue adding pieces while seeking another elusive Super Bowl run?

The Cowboys have been more aggressive in adding pieces, with last season's Quinnen Williams trade good evidence of that. Owner Jerry Jones has hinted in recent months that there are marquee players they could make a run at. Dallas sent its first-rounder to the Jets for Williams, but the Micah Parsons trade sends a first back to the Cowboys in 2027, and they also have extra Day 3 picks next year to dangle.

The defense had a long night Sunday, and cornerback feels especially thin behind DaRon Bland, with Cobie Durant and Shavon Revel next in the pecking order. The recent injury to safety Malik Hooker has hurt the overall secondary prowess, too.

They have the cap space and motivation to make a move, and the Cowboys and Steelers have been frequent trade partners the past few years, with the George Pickens and Broderick Jones deals. This is one to keep an eye on if the Cowboys are willing to part with the draft picks.

If you watched the Bears' Week 1 demolition of the Panthers, you know they have what could be a special offense. Defensively, however, things are less settled. They allowed 37 points at Carolina, giving up four receptions of 27 yards or longer, including a 51-yard TD pass.

The Bears also check the scheme box. They were on the higher end of the man-coverage spectrum last season and appeared to play an even higher percentage in Week 1. Porter and Jaylon Johnson would make a fine pair, and the depth is a bit sparse thereafter, but can the team afford to pay two corners more than $50 million next season?

They also have more immediate constraints, sitting less than $5 million under the cap for this season, and the Bears have recently extended several key pieces. Fitting Porter into the financial structure — with a Caleb Williams extension possibly looming next offseason — is the real trick here.

The Bears could try to steal a player of Porter's caliber from a division rival, but there are some hoops to jump through to make that happen.

The Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia was a reminder that when the 49ers are at their best — and healthiest — they can match almost any team's best. But in the thorny NFC West, nothing can be taken for granted, and the Niners might have to be aggressive to make a run at the division title and, ultimately, a return trip to the Super Bowl.

If the 49ers decide Porter makes sense, they'll have the financial flexibility to do it. The Niners lead the league in salary-cap space currently, and GM John Lynch has earned his "Trader John" nickname with in-season moves for players such as Christian McCaffrey, Jimmy Garoppolo, Chase Young, Emmanuel Sanders and others. If a player is deemed a good fit, they're absolutely willing to listen.

But therein lies the hangup: The Niners remain a heavier zone-coverage team, so the question remains whether Porter and his expensive cost would be worth the acquisition.

Needs-wise, however, Porter could be viewed as an upgrade over Renardo Green, and a top pairing of Porter and Deommodore Lenoir would give them better length and skill to match the battery of talented receivers they're set to face this season.

There has been some speculation surrounding Porter and the Commanders, and on a few levels it makes sense.

If you watched the Week 1 loss to the Eagles, you likely saw a few coverage busts from Mike Sainristil on the outside. He's a better fit inside, and acquiring Porter would allow that move to happen. The Commanders say they still like 2025 second-round pick Trey Amos, but he has practiced in full just once since Nov. 9 last year, so his ongoing injury concerns keep him a risky-at-best fallback option at some point.

Their supple cap situation probably makes a Porter trade financially viable, too, even if they're earmarking a lot of money for Jayden Daniels' future extension.

But would GM Adam Peters be willing to part with more valuable draft pieces? That strategy, trading for Laremy Tunsil and Deebo Samuel in 2025, hasn't paid off yet, and it left them with a shallow draft till the past two years, making only 11 draft picks (and only four on Days 1 and 2). Biting into their future picks could lead to similar problems and a shallower depth chart.

The Commanders can use the high-end talent on defense, but this is not a man-heavy scheme that perfectly fits Porter's skill set, and the cost might ultimately be a bit out of reach if there's a strong market for his services.

articles.title: Bills’ Josh Allen predicted to win MVP after Week 1
articles.summary: Josh Allen’s strong start to the 2026 NFL season has put the Buffalo Bills quarterback in the MVP conversation.
articles.body:
Josh Allen opened the 2026 NFL season with another standout performance for the Buffalo Bills . The quarterback helped Buffalo earn a Week 1 win over the Houston Texans , delivering a big performance in a close game.

Allen completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns, finishing with a 130.5 passer rating. His performance helped the Bills overcome Houston on the road and gave the team an early boost in the AFC.

The season is still young, but Allen has already drawn attention in the race for the NFL's most prestigious individual award. He won the MVP honor in 2024, and his latest performance has renewed discussion about whether he can claim it again.

Russell Wilson predicts Josh Allen to win NFL MVP

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images

Former NFL quaterback Russell Wilson predicted Josh Allen to win the 2026 NFL MVP award after his impressive Week 1 performance. The prediction puts the Buffalo Bills quarterback among the early names to watch in the award race.

Allen's opening game offered a strong argument for his candidacy. He produced through the air and on the ground, giving the Bills a reliable source of offense in a challenging road matchup.

However, one game does not decide the MVP race. Allen will need to maintain that level of play as the season continues, while other players make their own cases.

Josh Allen and the Bills look to build on Week 1 win

Buffalo will now turn its attention to its Week 2 matchup against the Detroit Lions . Allen's performance against Houston gives the team a positive starting point, but the Bills still have a long season ahead.

The quarterback's ability to make plays as both a passer and runner remains central to Buffalo's offense. If he continues to produce at a high level and helps the Bills keep winning, the MVP conversation is likely to follow him throughout the season.

For now, Russell Wilson has made its early prediction. Allen's next performances will determine how strong that case becomes.
